assets.label: Metal Gear MSX2 — chien de garde, profil natif
assets.targetFrame: DOG group, upper row, first horizontal side-profile frame at approximately x124–156/y10–27 of the original 420×273 sheet.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one individual transparent pixel-art creature sprite for a Metal Gear MSX2 visual atlas.
Input image 1 is a native extraction sheet from the original Metal Gear MSX2 game, used only as a design reference.
Target ONLY the first horizontal side-profile guard dog in the DOG section at the very top: the frame approximately at x124–156, y10–27 of the 420×273 reference, immediately to the right of the four upright-looking dog frames. It is the left-facing side-profile dog, NOT the sleeping dog at the extreme left, not a human guard and not any other animation frame.
Reconstruct ONE complete isolated enlarged pixel-art version of that exact observed dog frame. Preserve its original compact body silhouette, left-facing head and muzzle, back, tail, leg positions and angular pixel-cluster arrangement. Keep the black body with the sparse muted copper/tan highlight pixels visible in the source. The tiny native sprite is the entire design authority. Do not reinterpret it as a realistic German Shepherd or redesign its anatomy.
Composition: one left-facing dog, complete muzzle, tail and all limbs inside a landscape transparent canvas with generous empty margins. Crisp square pixel-art blocks, no smooth painted fur and no new material textures. Keep the source pose and elevated native viewing angle.
Remove the sheet's magenta tiles, red backdrop, frame lines and lettering. No collar, harness, leash, military armor, eyes or facial detail beyond the source, no extra dog, person, second frame, floor, shadow, effects, words, checkerboard or border. Output ONE PNG on a genuinely transparent alpha background.

assets.label: Metal Gear NES — chien de garde, profil natif
assets.targetFrame: DOG group, upper row, first horizontal side-profile frame at approximately x124–156/y10–27 of the original 255×211 sheet.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one individual transparent pixel-art creature sprite for the Metal Gear NES visual atlas.
Input image 1 is the native extraction sheet from Metal Gear on NES, used only as a design reference. This specific NES frame is the authority; do not substitute an MSX2 dog.
Target ONLY the first horizontal side-profile dog in the DOG section at the top: approximately x124–156, y10–27 of the 255×211 reference sheet, immediately to the right of the four upright-looking dog frames. Use that one left-facing running/crouched side-profile frame, not the sleeping dogs at the far left and not a different frame.
Reconstruct ONE enlarged isolated pixel-art rendering of that complete NES guard dog. Preserve its angular compact silhouette, left-facing head and muzzle, black back and body, native leg positions and tail, and the sparse pale beige/tan and gray highlight pixels. Preserve exactly the character of the limited NES palette and the elevated native view. Do not transform the tiny source into a realistically detailed dog or add fur texture.
Composition: one entire left-facing dog on a landscape transparent canvas; keep muzzle, tail and every source limb inside generous margins. Crisp square pixel blocks and no painted gradients. One pose only.
Remove all magenta tiles, red background, dividing lines and text from the sheet. No collar, harness, leash, armor, extra facial features, person, extra animal, alternate view, floor, cast shadow, smoke, HUD, frame, watermark or checkerboard. Output ONE PNG with genuine transparent alpha around the entire silhouette.

assets.label: Metal Gear NES — garde au jetpack, pose native
assets.targetFrame: JETPACK GUARD group, first complete guard frame at the lower-left, approximately x1–18/y144–173 of the 255×211 sheet.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one individual transparent character sprite for the Metal Gear NES visual atlas.
Input image 1 is the native sprite extraction sheet from the original Metal Gear NES port. Use only the FIRST full guard frame immediately under the JETPACK GUARD heading at the lower left of the sheet, approximately x1–18, y144–173 of the 255×211 source. Ignore the ordinary GUARD section, dogs, cameras, scorpions and roller.
Primary request: create ONE isolated enlarged pixel-art rendering of that exact jetpack guard frame. Preserve the compact upright human silhouette, the original helmet/head shape, shoulders and arms, narrow waist, native leg and foot arrangement, and the visible jetpack/back-equipment shapes. Preserve the small black, pale cream and tan NES palette and angular pixel-cluster construction. The native frame is the whole design reference; do not invent hidden machinery.
Composition: one whole figure centered head to feet on a portrait transparent canvas, same native facing/view and pose, with generous transparent margins. Crisp uniform square pixel-art blocks, no realistic soldier redesign, no photorealistic texture, no new armor plating or newly detailed face.
No visible jet flame, smoke, flight trail or muzzle flash unless contained in the selected native frame; the chosen frame is a quiet static pose. No new weapon design, markings, insignia, modern tactical gear, second character, sheet or alternate frame. Remove the magenta tile, red sheet backdrop, borders, labels and all other objects. No floor, cast shadow, UI, text, logo, opaque background or checkerboard. Exactly one PNG with true transparent alpha.

assets.label: Metal Gear MSX2 — garde rouge d’Outer Heaven
assets.targetFrame: GUARDS group, first red-uniform guard of the top row after the six gray guard frames, approximately x124–140/y56–88.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one individual transparent character sprite for the original Metal Gear MSX2 visual atlas.
Input image 1 is a native sprite extraction sheet, a design reference only. Target ONLY the first red-uniform guard frame in the top row of the GUARDS section: immediately after the six gray guard frames, approximately x124–140/y56–88 in the 420×273 sheet. Use this exact red guard pose, not the gray, blue or green variants, and not the NES version.
Create ONE complete enlarged pixel-art reconstruction of that native red guard. Preserve the source's compact proportions, slightly elevated native viewpoint, head covering, pose, visible arms, equipment shapes, legs and boots, and the red/black/tan pixel palette. Retain the original silhouette and pixel-cluster appearance; no conversion into a new realistic military character.
Composition: one complete head-to-boots figure centered on a portrait transparent canvas with generous margin on every side. The exact facing and posture of the selected frame are retained. Crisp consistent square pixel blocks; no smooth shading, new texture, invented facial detail, pouches, insignia, body armor, rifle attachments or backpack details.
Do not copy the red sheet backdrop, magenta tile, dividing lines, labels or any other sprite. No extra pose, duplicate guard, montage, contact sheet, border, ground, shadow, text, watermark, colored background or checkerboard. Exactly one PNG with genuine transparent alpha outside the character.
Reference routing: of the five supplied recent conversation images, use ONLY the FIRST image, the original 420×273 MSX2 native sprite sheet, for this red guard. The second image is the NES sheet and the remaining images are previous outputs of other targets; ignore those for the design. This is a new MSX2 red guard asset.
